correctness.rationale: Reconstructed finite splitting Fourier transform: for every character chi, hat(uv)(chi)=hat u(chi o phi)hat v(chi o (1-phi)), so commuting is a determinant-zero condition on each edge of the T=phi^-1(1-phi) character cycles. The q^2-vertex compatibility matrix has eigenvalues 0 with multiplicity (q+1)(q-2), q-1 with multiplicity q, and the two roots lambda^2-q lambda-q(q-1)=0; trace of powers gives U_m(q)+q(q-1)^m and products over independent cycles give every ordered commuting-pair count. The fixed-vector centralizer constraints give the stated run/zero-run dimension rule, including m=1, m=2, all-zero and all-nonzero boundaries. Universal commuting center is supported precisely on T-fixed characters, counted by |ker(1-2phi)|; Möbius inversion gives cycle counts. I independently enumerated *both* vectors for (q,m)=(2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3),(5,2): exact pair totals 4,10,22,33,105,145 and matching all first-vector centralizer dimensions. These finite checks supplement rather than prove the unrestricted field/group statement.
